pages.text: During science class, Akrofi asked, “Does sugar dissolve faster in warm water or in cold water?” Madam Salamatu smiled. “That is a great question to investigate, Akrofi. Let us test it—and make sure our test is fair.”
sentences: During science class, Akrofi asked, “Does sugar dissolve faster in warm water or in cold water?” Madam Salamatu smiled.
“That is a great question to investigate, Akrofi.
Let us test it—and make sure our test is fair.”
pages.alt: At a science table with two clear cups, Akrofi looks curiously toward Madam Salamatu while Lekettey stands beside him.

pages.text: Akrofi’s first try was not fair. He put a heaped spoonful of sugar into warm water and a tiny pinch into cold water, and he stirred only the warm cup for a long time. “The sugar in the warm cup vanished first,” he said, “yet I cannot tell why.”
sentences: Akrofi’s first try was not fair.
He put a heaped spoonful of sugar into warm water and a tiny pinch into cold water, and he stirred only the warm cup for a long time.
“The sugar in the warm cup vanished first,” he said, “yet I cannot tell why.”
pages.alt: Akrofi stirring a cup of water vigorously while a heaped spoon, a tiny pinch of sugar, and an unstirred second cup sit unevenly on the desk.

pages.text: Madam Salamatu held up one finger. “You changed three things at once: the amount of sugar, the stirring, and the warmth of the water,” she explained. “In a fair test, we change only one thing and keep everything else the same.”
sentences: Madam Salamatu held up one finger.
“You changed three things at once: the amount of sugar, the stirring, and the warmth of the water,” she explained.
“In a fair test, we change only one thing and keep everything else the same.”
pages.alt: Madam Salamatu smiling kindly and holding up exactly one index finger as Akrofi and Lekettey listen closely.

pages.text: Akrofi tried again carefully. He poured the exact same amount of water into two matching clear cups—one with warm tap water and one with cold water. He added one level spoonful of sugar to each cup and stirred both ten times while Lekettey timed them with his watch.
sentences: He poured the exact same amount of water into two matching clear cups—one with warm tap water and one with cold water.
He added one level spoonful of sugar to each cup and stirred both ten times while Lekettey timed them with his watch.
pages.alt: Akrofi measuring two identical clear cups of water with equal level spoons of sugar while Lekettey checks his wristwatch beside him.

pages.text: The sugar in the warm tap water disappeared first. Akrofi did the exact same test three times, and the warm cup won every single time. “Repeating a test makes us much more sure of our answer,” said Madam Salamatu.
sentences: The sugar in the warm tap water disappeared first.
Akrofi did the exact same test three times, and the warm cup won every single time.
“Repeating a test makes us much more sure of our answer,” said Madam Salamatu.
pages.alt: On the classroom table stand three neat pairs of matching clear cups, with Akrofi and Lekettey smiling as Madam Salamatu nods approvingly.

pages.text: In his notebook, Akrofi recorded that sugar dissolves faster in warm water than in cold water. “My first try did not work,” he smiled, “yet it taught me how to do a fair test!” Remember: children use warm tap water, and hot water is only for adults.
sentences: In his notebook, Akrofi recorded that sugar dissolves faster in warm water than in cold water.

pages.alt: Akrofi writing neatly with his pencil in an unlabelled open notebook at his desk, beaming with pride beside Lekettey.
